s.en: Network exploration tool and security / port scanner
s.es: escáner de red: descubre equipos, puertos abiertos, servicios y sistemas operativos

p.es: Equipo(s) a escanear: IP, nombre, rango (10.0.0.1-50) o red (192.168.1.0/24).
p.en: Host(s) to scan: IP, name, range (10.0.0.1-50) or network (192.168.1.0/24).

tip: Escanear redes que no son tuyas sin permiso escrito es ilegal. Para empezar: «nmap -sV -T4 equipo».

o.es: Escaneo SYN (semiabierto, «sigiloso»): envía SYN y no completa la conexión. Requiere root.
o.en: SYN scan (half-open, "stealth"): sends SYN and does not complete the connection. Needs root.

o.es: Escaneo TCP connect: completa la conexión (no necesita root, más ruidoso).
o.en: TCP connect scan: completes the connection (no root needed, noisier).

o.es: Escaneo UDP (lento).
o.en: UDP scan (slow).

o.es: Detecta el servicio y la versión de cada puerto abierto.
o.en: Probe open ports to determine service/version info.

o.es: Ejecuta los scripts NSE por defecto (equivale a --script=default).
o.en: Run the default NSE scripts (same as --script=default).

o.es: Solo descubre equipos activos (ping scan), sin escanear puertos.
o.en: Only discover live hosts (ping scan), no port scan.

o.es: Escaneo ACK: sirve para mapear reglas de cortafuegos.
o.en: ACK scan: used to map firewall rulesets.

o.es: Escaneos NULL, FIN y Xmas: banderas TCP inusuales para saltarse filtros simples.
o.en: NULL, FIN and Xmas scans: unusual TCP flags to slip past simple filters.

o.es: Escaneo «idle» a través de un equipo zombi (no ves tu IP en el objetivo).
o.en: Idle scan via a zombie host (your IP is not seen by the target).

o.es: Solo lista los objetivos sin enviar nada.
o.en: List targets only without sending anything.

o.es: Intenta detectar el sistema operativo.
o.en: Enable OS detection.

o.es: Modo agresivo: -O -sV -sC y traceroute.
o.en: Aggressive mode: -O -sV -sC and traceroute.

o.es: Todos los puertos (1-65535).
o.en: All ports (1-65535).

o.es: Escaneo rápido: los 100 puertos más comunes.
o.en: Fast: scan the 100 most common ports.

o.es: Escanea los N puertos más comunes.
o.en: Scan the N most common ports.

o.es: No hace ping previo: trata todos los equipos como activos (útil si bloquean ICMP).
o.en: Skip host discovery: treat all hosts as up (useful when ICMP is blocked).

o.es: No resuelve DNS (más rápido y menos ruido).
o.en: Never do DNS resolution.

o.es: Resuelve DNS siempre.
o.en: Always resolve DNS.

o.es: Velocidad (plantilla de tiempos): 0 paranoico … 3 normal … 4 agresivo, 5 loco.
o.en: Timing template: 0 paranoid … 3 normal … 4 aggressive, 5 insane.

o.es: Guarda el resultado en texto normal.
o.en: Save output in normal format.

o.es: Guarda el resultado en XML.
o.en: Save output in XML format.

o.es: Guarda en formato «grepable».
o.en: Save in grepable format.

o.es: Guarda en los tres formatos (BASE.nmap, .xml y .gnmap).
o.en: Save in all three formats (BASE.nmap, .xml and .gnmap).

o.es: Más detalle (-vv aún más).
o.en: Increase verbosity level.

o.es: Depuración (-dd aún más).
o.en: Increase debugging level.

o.es: Lee los objetivos de un archivo.
o.en: Input from list of hosts/networks.

o.es: Excluye equipos o redes del escaneo.
o.en: Exclude hosts/networks.

o.es: Muestra solo los puertos abiertos.
o.en: Only show open (or possibly open) ports.

o.es: Muestra por qué se considera cada puerto en ese estado.
o.en: Display the reason a port is in a particular state.

o.es: Ejecuta scripts NSE: nombres, categorías (vuln, safe, auth, exploit, brute…) o rutas.
o.en: Run NSE scripts: names, categories (vuln, safe, auth, exploit, brute…) or paths.

o.es: Argumentos para los scripts NSE.
o.en: Provide arguments to NSE scripts.

o.es: Traza la ruta hasta cada equipo.
o.en: Trace hop path to each host.

o.es: Usa esta interfaz de red.
o.en: Use specified interface.

o.es: Disfraza el escaneo con direcciones señuelo.
o.en: Cloak a scan with decoys.

o.es: Suplanta la dirección de origen.
o.en: Spoof source address.

o.es: Usa ese puerto de origen (para saltar filtros).
o.en: Use given port number as source.

o.es: Fragmenta los paquetes (para evadir detección).
o.en: Fragment packets.

o.es: MTU personalizado para la fragmentación.
o.en: Use specified MTU for fragmentation.

o.es: Añade N bytes aleatorios a los paquetes.
o.en: Append random data to sent packets.

o.es: Mezcla el orden de los objetivos.
o.en: Randomize target scan order.

o.es: Envía al menos N paquetes por segundo.
o.en: Send packets no slower than N per second.

o.es: Envía como mucho N paquetes por segundo.
o.en: Send packets no faster than N per second.

o.es: Reintentos por puerto.
o.en: Caps number of port scan probe retransmissions.

o.es: Abandona un equipo tras ese tiempo.
o.en: Give up on target after this long.

o.es: Espera entre sondeos (evita detección).
o.en: Adjust delay between probes.

o.es: Escaneo IPv6.
o.en: Enable IPv6 scanning.

o.es: Descubrimiento con ICMP echo.
o.en: ICMP echo discovery probes.

o.es: Descubrimiento con TCP SYN a esos puertos.
o.en: TCP SYN discovery to given ports.

o.es: Descubrimiento con TCP ACK.
o.en: TCP ACK discovery to given ports.

o.es: Descubrimiento con UDP.
o.en: UDP discovery to given ports.

o.es: Descubrimiento ARP (solo red local).
o.en: ARP discovery (local network only).

o.es: Escaneo de rebote FTP.
o.en: FTP bounce scan.

o.es: No aleatoriza el orden de los puertos.
o.en: Scan ports consecutively - don't randomize.

o.es: Reanuda un escaneo interrumpido.
o.en: Resume an aborted scan.

o.es: Hoja de estilo XSL para el XML.
o.en: Use XSL stylesheet to transform XML output.

o.es: Muestra la versión.
o.en: Print version number.
<Lua scripts> is a comma-separated list of script-files or script-categories.

If a hostname target resolves to more than one address, scan all of them. The default behavior is to only scan the first resolved address. Regardless, only addresses in the appropriate address family will be scanned: IPv4 by default, IPv6 with -6.

Scan each IP address only once. The default behavior is to scan each address as many times as it is specified in the target list, such as when network ranges overlap or different hostnames resolve to the same address.

This option sends an SCTP packet containing a minimal INIT chunk. The default destination port is 80 (configurable at compile time by changing DEFAULT_SCTP_PROBE_PORT_SPEC in nmap.h). Alternate ports can be specified as a parameter. The syntax is the same as for the -p except that port type specifiers like S: are not allowed.

Nmap normally does ARP or IPv6 Neighbor Discovery (ND) discovery of locally connected ethernet hosts, even if other host discovery options such as -Pn or -PE are used. To disable this implicit behavior, use the --disable-arp-ping option.

In some cases, firewalls may spoof TCP reset (RST) replies in response to probes to unoccupied or disallowed addresses. Since Nmap ordinarily considers RST replies to be proof that the target is up, this can lead to wasted time scanning targets that aren't there.

SCTP[6] is a relatively new alternative to the TCP and UDP protocols, combining most characteristics of TCP and UDP, and also adding new features like multi-homing and multi-streaming. It is mostly being used for SS7/SIGTRAN related services but has the potential to be used for other applications as well.

Window scan is exactly the same as ACK scan except that it exploits an implementation detail of certain systems to differentiate open ports from closed ones, rather than always printing unfiltered when a RST is returned. It does this by examining the TCP Window field of the RST packets returned.

The Maimon scan is named after its discoverer, Uriel Maimon. He described the technique in Phrack Magazine issue #49 (November 1996). Nmap, which included this technique, was released two issues later. This technique is exactly the same as NULL, FIN, and Xmas scans, except that the probe is FIN/ACK.

SCTP COOKIE ECHO scan is a more advanced SCTP scan. It takes advantage of the fact that SCTP implementations should silently drop packets containing COOKIE ECHO chunks on open ports, but send an ABORT if the port is closed. The advantage of this scan type is that it is not as obvious a port scan than an INIT scan.

By default, Nmap version detection skips TCP port 9100 because some printers simply print anything sent to that port, leading to dozens of pages of HTTP GET requests, binary SSL session requests, etc.

When Nmap performs OS detection against a target and fails to find a perfect match, it usually repeats the attempt. By default, Nmap tries five times if conditions are favorable for OS fingerprint submission, and twice when conditions aren't so good.

Nmap has the ability to port scan or version scan multiple hosts in parallel. Nmap does this by dividing the target IP space into groups and then scanning one group at a time. In general, larger groups are more efficient. The downside is that host results can't be provided until the whole group is finished.

These options control the total number of probes that may be outstanding for a host group. They are used for port scanning and host discovery. By default, Nmap calculates an ever-changing ideal parallelism based on network performance. If packets are being dropped, Nmap slows down and allows fewer outstanding probes.

Nmap maintains a running timeout value for determining how long it will wait for a probe response before giving up or retransmitting the probe. This is calculated based on the response times of previous probes. If the network latency shows itself to be significant and variable, this timeout can grow to several seconds.

While some scripts complete in fractions of a second, others can take hours or more depending on the nature of the script, arguments passed in, network and application conditions, and more. The --script-timeout option sets a ceiling on script execution time.

Many hosts have long used rate limiting to reduce the number of ICMP error messages (such as port-unreachable errors) they send. Some systems now apply similar rate limits to the RST (reset) packets they generate. This can slow Nmap down dramatically as it adjusts its timing to reflect those rate limits.
Similar to --defeat-rst-ratelimit, the --defeat-icmp-ratelimit option trades accuracy for speed, increasing UDP scanning speed against hosts that rate-limit ICMP error messages.

Enforce use of a given nsock IO multiplexing engine. Only the select(2)-based fallback engine is guaranteed to be available on your system. Engines are named after the name of the IO management facility they leverage. Engines currently implemented are epoll, kqueue, poll, and select, but not all will be present on any platform.

Asks Nmap to use the deprecated Adler32 algorithm for calculating the SCTP checksum. If --adler32 is not given, CRC-32C (Castagnoli) is used. RFC 2960[13] originally defined Adler32 as checksum algorithm for SCTP; RFC 4960[6] later redefined the SCTP checksums to use CRC-32C.
Script kiddie output is like interactive output, except that it is post-processed to better suit the l33t HaXXorZ who previously looked down on Nmap due to its consistent capitalization and spelling.

Periodically prints a timing status message after each interval of time. The time is a specification of the kind described in the section called “TIMING AND PERFORMANCE”; so for example, use --stats-every 10s to get a status update every 10 seconds. Updates are printed to interactive output (the screen) and XML output.

Asks Nmap to use the specified services file rather than the nmap-services data file that comes with Nmap. Using this option also causes a fast scan (-F) to be used. See the description for --datadir for more information on Nmap's data files.
Asks Nmap to use the specified service probes file rather than the nmap-service-probes data file that comes with Nmap. See the description for --datadir for more information on Nmap's data files.
Asks Nmap to send packets at the raw ethernet (data link) layer rather than the higher IP (network) layer. By default, Nmap chooses the one which is generally best for the platform it is running on.
Asks Nmap to send packets via raw IP sockets rather than sending lower level ethernet frames. It is the complement to the --send-eth option discussed previously.

This option is only useful for memory-leak debugging. It causes Nmap to release allocated memory just before it quits so that actual memory leaks are easier to spot. Normally Nmap skips this as the OS does this anyway upon process termination. Prints the Nmap version number and exits.
